[# [论文评述] GNN-ACLP: Graph Neural Networks based Analog Circuit Link Prediction](/file? url=https%3A%2F%2Farxiv.org%2Fpdf%2F2504.10240). 本文提出了一种基于图神经网络 (GNN) 的模拟电路连接预测框架 GNN-ACLP，旨在解决现有方法在模拟电路自动设计中面临的挑战，即：电路图拓扑模式利用不足导致预测精度低、数据稀缺限制模型泛化能力以及对各种网表格式的适应性有限。. 1. **SEAL 框架的应用：** 将电路连接预测问题建模为无向图连接预测问题，其中节点代表电路元件的端口，边代表端口之间的连接。利用 SEAL (Subgraphs, Embeddings, and Attributes for Link Prediction) 框架，通过提取链接周围的子图来获取训练数据。为了有效识别子图中节点的不同角色并保留结构信息，采用了 Double-Radius Node Labeling (DRNL) 节点标记方法，并结合原始元件节点特征进行训练，从而实现端口级别的连接预测精度。具体来说，对于一对节点 (x, y)，包含子图被定义为包含 x 和 y 的 h-hop 邻域的子图。DRNL 的目标是在保留结构信息的同时识别节点的不同角色。. 2. **Netlist Babel Fish：** 开发了一个名为 Netlist Babel Fish 的网表格式转换工具，利用检索增强生成 (RAG) 与大型语言模型 (LLM) 相结合，实现了网表格式的双向转换。该工具集成了包含 SPICE 器件和语句简要参考、网表处理方法、支持的元件库及端口分配规范以及实例的结构化 SPICE 知识库，从而增强了网表格式的兼容性。DeepSeek V2.5 被用作 LLM。该系统通过解耦的知识表示框架实现可扩展性，其中特定于格式的转换规则被显式编码而不是隐式学习。. 3. **SpiceNetlist 数据集：** 构建了一个包含 775 个带标注电路的综合数据集 SpiceNetlist，涵盖 10 种不同的元件类别，数据同时具有 SPICE 和 JSON 格式，用于支持电路连接预测方法的训练和评估。通过一个鲁棒的预处理流程来检测和纠正四个 SPICE 网表数据集中的内容错误和语法不一致性。具体来说，PySpice 用于自动检测和过滤具有语法不一致性的 SPICE 网表。随后，使用 Netlist Babel Fish 将所有数据集转换为 JSON 格式，并进行手动验证，以识别和纠正两种格式中具有内容错误的网表。. 实验结果表明，GNN-ACLP 在 SpiceNetlist 数据集上比现有方法提高了 15.05%，在 Image2Net 数据集上提高了 12.01%。. * GNN-ACLP，一种基于 GNN 的端口级精确电路连接预测方法，它使用了 SEAL 框架。. * Netlist Babel Fish，一种网表格式转换器，通过 RAG 实现了基于 LLM 的解释，从而实现了跨多种格式的端口级网表解析。. * SpiceNetlist，一个新的电路网表数据集，包含 775 个 SPICE 和 JSON 格式的带注释电路，具有 10 种组件类型，以方便电路连接预测方法的训练和评估。. ## 免费AI PDF查看器 革新您的论文阅读方式. / CEO Younghyun Chung / Business Registration Number 271-86-02206. 34, Yeongdong-daero 85-gil, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea, 06180. results.title: GNN-ACLP: Graph Neural Networks based Analog Circuit Link Prediction
results.content: To address these challenges, we propose GNN-ACLP, a GNNs-based method for analog circuit link prediction, as illustrated in Figure 1, and SpiceNetlist, a large-scale netlist dataset, whose statistic is demonstrated in Table 1. GNN-ACLP, a port-level accurate circuit link prediction method based on the SEAL framework using graph neural networks (GNNs). SpiceNetlist, a novel circuit netlist dataset comprising 775 annotated circuits in both SPICE and JSON formats, featuring 10 component types to facilitate the training and evaluation of circuit link prediction methods. We adopt the SEAL framework for link prediction in circuit graphs and train it using DRNL one-hot encoding combined with the original component node features. For the circuit-link-prediction problem, there are very few datasets available, and the existing ones do not contain enough readily accessible netlists for practical training and evaluation. We propose GNN-ACLP, a novel graph neural networks based framework with SEAL framework integration and achieve port-level accuracy in analog circuit link prediction.

results.title: [2504.10240] Graph Neural Networks Based Analog Circuit Link Prediction
results.content: # Title:Graph Neural Networks Based Analog Circuit Link Prediction. View a PDF of the paper titled Graph Neural Networks Based Analog Circuit Link Prediction, by Guanyuan Pan and 8 other authors. > Abstract:Circuit link prediction, which identifies missing component connections from incomplete netlists, is crucial in analog circuit design automation. However, existing methods face three main challenges: 1) Insufficient use of topological patterns in circuit graphs reduces prediction accuracy; 2) Data scarcity due to the complexity of annotations hinders model generalization; 3) Limited adaptability to various netlist formats restricts model flexibility. We propose Graph Neural Networks Based Analog Circuit Link Prediction (GNN-ACLP), a graph neural networks (GNNs) based method featuring three innovations to tackle these challenges. |  | (or  arXiv:2504.10240v5 [cs.AR] for this version) |. results.content: # hERG-toxicity prediction using traditional machine learning and advanced deep learning techniques. GNN is free of any feature engineering steps and has minimal human interventions. GNN may serve as a basis for comprehensive automation of predictive toxicology. ## Abstract. Our study demonstrates utilization of traditional machine learning techniques such as random forest (RF), support-vector machine (SVM), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), deep neural network (DNN) as well as advanced deep learning techniques like gated recurrent unit-based DNN (GRU-DNN) and graph neural network (GNN), towards predicting human ether-á-go-go related gene (hERG) derived toxicity. The GNN was found to be the top performing model based on predictive power and generalizability. The GNN technique is free of any feature engineering steps while having a minimal human intervention. The GNN approach may serve as a basis for comprehensive automation in predictive toxicology. ## Graphical abstract. ## Data availability.
